We need to interpret the problem. We are agent B. We must choose exactly one task for ourselves. The scenario: fresh allocation round, all tasks initially unclaimed. A and B choose simultaneously, not seeing each other's choice. Then C and D choose two distinct unclaimed tasks minimizing combined execution cost, tie-breaking lexicographically by (C-task, D-task). The shared objective: maximize number of distinct tasks completed, then minimize total execution cost across all four agents. A and B have same objective and tie-break rule: among rows that maximize distinct tasks and then minimize total cost, select lexicographically smallest (A-task, B-task) pair, comparing task IDs lexicographically in A-then-B order. Each agent must choose the component for its own role. So we need to decide B's task given that we know A will also be following same rule. The public outcome table lists all possible A/B choices and resulting C/D choices (presumably following the minimization rule). We need to select the row(s) that maximize distinct tasks completed, then minimize total execution cost, then tie-break by lexicographically smallest (A,B) pair. Then B must choose its task accordingly.

Now tie-break rule: Among rows that maximize distinct tasks and minimize total cost, select lexicographically smallest (A-task, B-task) pair, comparing task IDs lexicographically in A-then-B order.
